candidates.title: Claude Opus 5.5 trades frontier capability for lower operating cost
candidates.summary: Anthropic's new Opus release targets high-end coding and agent work while cutting operating cost and adding stronger safeguards after recent containment incidents.
candidates.what_changed: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 as the first model in its 5.5 family, positioning it near its highest-capability tier while reducing operating cost relative to Opus 5.
candidates.why_it_matters: Frontier releases are increasingly competing on **price-performance and operational safety**, not benchmark scores alone.

candidates.title: GitHub Copilot exports agent traces through OpenTelemetry
candidates.summary: Enterprise admins can send model and tool spans from Copilot agent sessions into existing observability systems through managed settings.
candidates.what_changed: GitHub Copilot now supports OpenTelemetry export configured through enterprise-managed settings. Teams can trace agent sessions, model requests, and tool interactions inside their existing monitoring stack.
candidates.why_it_matters: Agent observability is converging on standard infrastructure instead of bespoke dashboards. That makes traces easier to correlate with application, security, and cost telemetry.

candidates.title: Copilot for JetBrains starts auto-approving low-risk tool calls
candidates.summary: GitHub's assisted approvals preview lets the agent clear low-risk tools automatically while preserving explicit prompts for higher-risk actions.
candidates.what_changed: Copilot for JetBrains 1.18 introduces assisted approvals: low-risk tool calls can be approved automatically, while higher-risk operations still require a human decision.
candidates.why_it_matters: This is a practical version of **risk-tiered autonomy**. Permission systems for coding agents are getting more granular than a binary “ask for everything” versus “full access.”
